title: Indian National Jailed for Life, Minimum 28 Years, for Airbnb Murder in London
excerpt: Deepak Sandhu, 24, murdered Xiaoqing Ke, 39, at her Earl's Court Airbnb after stealing £500 from her, the Old Bailey heard. He was convicted of murder and perverting the course of justice and arrested on a coach while trying to flee the country.
body:
• Deepak Sandhu, 24, an Indian national, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 28 years at the Old Bailey on Friday for the murder of Xiaoqing Ke, 39.
  • Ms Ke was found face down in her Airbnb bedsit on Old Brompton Road, Earl's Court, on December 10 last year, with catastrophic injuries including a fatal stab wound to the neck.
  • Prosecutors said Sandhu, a university dropout who had posed as a model and actor, stole £500 from Ms Ke and killed her in a planned revenge attack after she rejected him.
  • A jury convicted him of murder and perverting the course of justice after about two hours of deliberation; he had been arrested on a coach while travelling to Birmingham Airport to flee the country.

An Indian national who murdered a woman at a London Airbnb in what prosecutors called a brutal and fatal revenge attack was jailed for life on Friday, with a minimum term of 28 years. Deepak Sandhu, 24, killed Xiaoqing Ke, 39, in Earl's Court in west London after buying knives in Asda, the Old Bailey was told, according to reporting of the sentencing.

The killing

Ms Ke, a single mother of two, was found face down on the bedroom floor of her Airbnb bedsit in Old Brompton Road on December 10 last year, with catastrophic injuries including a deep, fatal stab wound to the neck. Prosecutor Caroline Carberry KC told the court that Sandhu, a failed AI student who claimed to be a model and actor, was a fantasist who had made false claims about his status and had stolen £500 from Ms Ke. The two had met while Ms Ke, a Mandarin speaker, was working in Southampton, where the Punjabi-speaking Sandhu was a customer; they conducted a secret relationship through a translation app. Sandhu travelled from Southampton to London after Ms Ke confronted him over the theft and her rejection of him.

"You took your revenge in a carefully planned and premeditated way."

— Judge Philip Katz KC, sentencing Deepak Sandhu

Lies, flight and verdict

Sandhu, whose student visa had been revoked after he dropped out of university in Southampton, denied responsibility and claimed Ms Ke was alive when he left her flat. A jury found him guilty of murder and of perverting the course of justice by attempting to flee the country, after deliberating for about two hours. He had been arrested on a coach while making his way to Birmingham Airport. Judge Philip Katz KC said Ms Ke had been kind and thoughtful toward Sandhu, and that he had repaid her by stealing her money and murdering her in a brutal and callous way; the lies Sandhu told, the judge said, were often manipulative, controlling and cruel.

The sentence

A life sentence with a 28-year minimum means Sandhu must serve at least 28 years before the Parole Board can consider his release, and he will remain on licence for life if he is ever freed. The case was prosecuted as a planned killing driven by rejection and a £500 theft — a dispute the Firstpost account of the verdict also centred on — rather than any wider dispute.
